channel.title: nu-metal on Loud Legends
channel.description: Recent content in nu-metal on Loud Legends

item.title: Watch LIMP BIZKIT’s FRED DURST Honor OZZY OSBOURNE And BLACK SABBATH With An Acoustic Cover Of 'CHANGES'
item.description: Limp Bizkit’s frontman Fred Durst delivered a surprising and heartfelt performance during the Back to the Beginning tribute to Ozzy Osbourne and Black Sabbath, even though he didn’t attend in person.

item.title: Disturbed's DAVID DRAIMAN On Crowd Reaction At Sabbath Farewell: 'A Few Jew Hating Morons'
item.description: Disturbed frontman David Draiman took the stage at Black Sabbath’s Back to the Beginning farewell event on July 5, held at Villa Park in Birmingham. What should have been a tribute moment turned into a noisy reception for the singer, who was booed by parts of the crowd before performing “Shot in the Dark” and “Sweet Leaf” as part of a rotating supergroup lineup.

item.title: KELLY OSBOURNE and SID WILSON Get Engaged at OZZY OSBOURNE’s Final BLACK SABBATH Concert; VIDEO
item.description: Kelly Osbourne and Sid Wilson are officially engaged. The couple marked the occasion in a memorable way, with the proposal happening backstage at none other than Ozzy Osbourne’s final concert with Black Sabbath.

item.title: SLIPKNOT Launches Cryptic Website With Countdown, Hints At 25th Anniversary Album Reissue
item.description: Slipknot is building anticipation with a cryptic online campaign that points toward a special 25th anniversary edition of their self-titled 1999 debut album. The band has launched a mysterious new website, 742617000027.

item.title: SOAD's SHAVO ODADJIAN Says Phone Bans At Shows 'Take Something Away' From Fans: 'I Catch Myself Filming Sometimes Too'
item.description: Shavo Odadjian, bassist of System of a Down, doesn’t believe in taking away your phone at a concert. In a recent Q&A with readers of Metal Hammer, Odadjian shared his thoughts on phone-free shows, a practice growing in popularity among artists looking to keep fans more engaged during live performances.

item.title: KALEN CHASE Explains Why VIMIC Won’t Continue Without JOEY JORDISON: 'There Are No Plans for Future Stuff'
item.description: VIMIC, the metal project formed by late Slipknot drummer Joey Jordison, is set to take the stage one last time. On October 3, the band will reunite for a tribute concert in Los Angeles.

item.title: How One EMBARRASSING Night at 'Whiskey A Go Go' Forced LINKIN PARK to Find CHESTER BENNINGTON
item.description: Linkin Park rose to become one of the most influential rock bands of the 21st century. Known for blending heavy guitar riffs, hip-hop beats, and electronic layers, the group built a sound that was both accessible and intense.

item.title: KITTIE’s Comeback Wasn’t Planned, Says MERCEDES LANDER: 'We Just Wanted To Play A Couple Shows'
item.description: Canadian metal band KITTIE is back with a new album, but the comeback wasn’t part of a grand plan. In a recent interview with Loud TV (transcribed by BLABBERMOUTH), drummer Mercedes Lander explained how the return came together almost by accident.

item.title: DEFTONES Tease Possible NEW SONG Or ALBUM Release With Cryptic Message During London Show
item.description: Deftones may be getting ready to release new music. During their concert at Crystal Palace Park in London on June 29, the band displayed a graphic on large screens near the stage.

item.title: Slipknot, Lamb of God, Anthrax Members Join Comic Con Birmingham Lineup
item.description: Comic Con is coming to Birmingham, and this year’s event will feature more than just movie and TV stars. Several well-known rock and metal musicians are set to appear, including members of Slipknot, Lamb of God, and Anthrax.

item.title: Every Song From SLIPKNOT’s SELF-TITLED Album Ranked From Worst To Best
item.description: Slipknot’s 1999 self-titled album was a game-changer. It introduced the world to nine masked musicians from Iowa who brought chaos, intensity, and something completely different to heavy music.

item.title: LIMP BIZKIT's WES BORLAND Cosplays As Skull-Faced JAMES HETFIELD At Metallica’s Denver Show
item.description: Limp Bizkit guitarist Wes Borland turned heads at Metallica’s Denver show on Friday by dressing up like a skull-faced version of 1980s James Hetfield (watch below). The look included a “Metal Up Your Ass” t-shirt and white high-top sneakers, all while performing a full 10-song set.

item.title: LIMP BIZKIT’s WES BORLAND’s Controversial Take on Heavy Metal: 'Boring As F*ck'
item.description: Wes Borland, guitarist for Limp Bizkit, has never exactly fit the mold of a typical nü-metal poster boy. Known for his elaborate stage costumes and artistic detours, Borland has always appeared slightly out of place next to Fred Durst’s red Yankees cap and the band’s frat-rap aggression.

item.title: KORN’s Full PINKPOP 2007 Performance With SLIPKNOT’s JOEY JORDISON Released On YouTube
item.description: A professionally filmed video of KORN’s full set at the Pinkpop Festival in the Netherlands — recorded on May 28, 2007 — has been made available online via the Pinkpop Archive YouTube channel.

item.title: HOLLYWOOD UNDEAD Releases Emotional New Single 'SAVIOR': 'We Can’t Wait For You To Hear It'
item.description: Rock group Hollywood Undead has dropped a new single titled “Savior” (watch it below), offering fans a more personal and emotional look at the band’s sound. The track is out now through Sumerian Records.

item.title: JACOBY SHADDIX Talks New PAPA ROACH Single With TOBY MORSE: 'It Felt Urgent, Honest, In Your Face'
item.description: Papa Roach is back with a new single, and they’ve brought along a longtime friend. The California rock band just released “Braindead” (watch it below), a high-energy track featuring Toby Morse, the lead singer of punk band H2O.

item.title: When MAX CAVALERA Almost Reunited With SEPULTURA: 'We'll Cross Paths Again'
item.description: Max Cavalera is best known for helping create one of Brazil’s most influential metal bands: Sepultura. But in 1996, after years of success, he walked away from it all.

item.title: LIMP BIZKIT's Top 5 Songs Ranked By Fans, From Deep Cuts To Major Hits
item.description: Limp Bizkit helped define the sound and attitude of late ’90s nu-metal. Known for mixing heavy guitars, rap vocals, and over-the-top energy, the band became one of the most talked-about acts of their time.

item.title: KITTIE’s MORGAN LANDER Talks About Writing 'FIRE': 'It Was A Relearning Curve'
item.description: Getting back in the studio after more than a decade isn’t as simple as picking up where you left off. Just ask Morgan Lander. The guitarist and vocalist for Canadian metal band KITTIE says that writing Fire, their first album in 13 years, didn’t come with muscle memory (via TotalRock).

item.title: Dave 'PHOENIX' Farrell Talks LINKIN PARK’s Return: 'Time Doesn’t Heal The Wound, It Changes The Lens'
item.description: Linkin Park is back on tour with a new album and new members. But for bassist Dave “Phoenix” Farrell, returning to the band after Chester Bennington’s death was not easy.

item.title: Evanescence's AMY LEE Reflects On Pandemic-Era Lessons: 'Who Knows When This Will Ever End? So Let’s Put Out Our Music'
item.description: Amy Lee says the pandemic changed how Evanescence approaches releasing music. In a recent interview with WDHA-FM, the singer explained that waiting for a perfect moment to drop a full album no longer feels realistic.

item.title: AMY LEE Says New EVANESCENCE Album Coming 'Probably Early Next Year'
item.description: Evanescence is working on their next studio album, and according to Amy Lee, it’s likely to arrive in early 2026. The singer gave an update during a recent interview with WDHA-FM 105.

item.title: Dave 'PHOENIX' Farrell Breaks Silence on CHESTER BENNINGTON’s Death: 'Is It Even Called LINKIN PARK Anymore?'
item.description: Linkin Park bassist Dave “Phoenix” Farrell opened up about the band’s long road back to music after the loss of lead singer Chester Bennington. In a new interview with Czech station Evropa 2 (transcribed by BLABBERMOUTH.

item.title: The Genre DAVE GROHL Called 'Too Easy' And Blamed for Making ROCK DUMBER
item.description: Dave Grohl has always been a believer in loud guitars, big feelings, and not overthinking things. Foo Fighters, the band he’s fronted since the mid-’90s, built a career on that formula: simple riffs, catchy choruses, and performances that sometimes go off the rails, in a good way.

item.title: Linkin Park’s EMILY ARMSTRONG Shaves Fan's Head on Stage at ROCK FOR PEOPLE 2025
item.description: Linkin Park opened their summer festival season with a big moment at Rock for People 2025. The band performed in front of 50,000 fans, but one person in the crowd definitely stood out.

item.title: Morgan Lander Says KITTIE May Release More Music: 'We’re Enjoying Ourselves'
item.description: KITTIE could be back in the studio again soon. Guitarist and vocalist Morgan Lander says the band is open to releasing more new music, thanks to the positive energy surrounding their recent reunion (transcribed by BLABBERMOUTH.

item.title: LINKIN PARK Cancels Switzerland Concert After Health Problem in Band: 'We’re Not In A Spot To Perform Tonight'
item.description: Linkin Park called off their performance in Bern, Switzerland just hours before showtime, citing a medical issue within the band. The June 20 concert at Bernexpo was part of the group’s 2025 world tour promoting From Zero, their first album since 2017.

item.title: Why Limp Bizkit’s FRED DURST Always Wore That RED BASEBALL CAP
item.description: Back in the early 2000s, nu metal was dominating the rock scene, with bands like Slipknot, Korn, Kid Rock, and Linkin Park in constant rotation on MTV.

item.title: The BEST SONG to Introduce Someone to KORN, According to JONATHAN DAVIS
item.description: So you want to introduce someone to Korn. Good luck. You’ve got nearly three decades’ worth of dreadlocks, detuned guitars, and unresolved childhood trauma to work with.

item.title: AMY LEE Talks About EMMA ANZAI Joining EVANESCENCE: 'I Called Her First'
item.description: Evanescence frontwoman Amy Lee has opened up about the band’s evolving lineup and her longtime connection with bassist Emma Anzai, offering rare insight into the decision-making behind the group’s most recent personnel shift.

item.title: When METALLICA Brought Back 'FRANTIC' Live And JAMES HETFIELD Roasted St. Anger
item.description: Back in 2021, Metallica briefly resurrected “Frantic”, the chaotic opener from their 2003 punching bag of an album, St. Anger. The band pulled the song out of retirement for a set at the Aftershock Festival on October 8 (watch the video below), years after it had mostly vanished from live shows following a few scattered appearances in 2019 and a much longer break since 2011.

item.title: EVANESCENCE's AMY LEE Joins Anti-Trump Protest in Nashville: 'Stop Kidnapping People'
item.description: Amy Lee from Evanescence was spotted at a protest in the U.S. taking a stand against Donald Trump’s immigration policies. The singer joined demonstrators in Nashville, where she lives, alongside her husband Josh Hartzler, both wearing t-shirts from the No Kings movement.

item.title: KORN Praises SLEEP TOKEN's Download Festival Show: 'They Outdid a SLIPKNOT Stage'
item.description: The members of Korn had high praise for Sleep Token following their performance at the Download Festival on Saturday, June 14. According to the band, the masked group managed to silence skeptics with a massive stage setup and commanding live presence.

item.title: The Day KORN Knocked a Guy Out Mid-Show… and Then WROTE A SONG About It
item.description: Not every song is born in a studio with clean instruments and sober minds. Some, like Korn’s Clown, crawl out of drug-fueled all-nighters in dingy apartments, shaped as much by the chaos around them as by the riffs themselves.

item.title: BRIAN WELCH on KORN's New Album: 'We're Doing It All On Tape'
item.description: Korn is back in the studio, but don’t expect any instant gratification. This time, they’re ditching modern convenience for a much older, sweatier process. During a chat with BBC Radio 1’s Rock Show With Daniel P Carter (as transcribed by The PRP, guitarist Brian “Head” Welch explained that the band has fully embraced analog recording.

item.title: Far-Right Politician Tries to Cancel SLIPKNOT and JUDAS PRIEST Shows in Italy
item.description: Alcide Mosso, a member of Italy’s far-right Lega Nord party, has launched an attack on the Ferrara Summer Festival, held throughout the summer in the city of Ferrara.

item.title: Is Slipknot Releasing a New Album in 2025? Here’s What We Know So Far
item.description: Slipknot fans are eagerly awaiting news of the band’s next studio album following 2022’s The End, So Far. While a new record hasn’t been officially announced, the band members have dropped numerous hints in recent interviews about their plans.

item.title: Disturbed & Megadeth Join Forces for The Sickness 25th-Anniversary Tour
item.description: Okay—stop what you’re doing—pause Love Island, put down the ghost pepper challenge, mute your ex’s chaotic MySpace playlist from 2008 (yes, it still plays in your head)—because we need to talk about DISTURBED and MEGADETH teaming up for a European tour in 2025… and frankly, the timeline has collapsed in on itself.

item.title: Clown Admits He Was a “Naysayer” About Revisiting Slipknot’s First Album
item.description: It’s 2025, and somehow Slipknot is still here, still wearing masks, still smashing percussion instruments like cavemen discovering fire, but also—shockingly—getting reflective about their past. Yes, you read that right: Shawn “Clown” Crahan, the band’s resident chaos conductor, actually sat down and got nostalgic.

item.title: Grammy Interviewer Mistakes Spiritbox’s Courtney LaPlante for Poppy—See the Full Video
item.description: Yeah babe, the Grammys. A night of glitz, glamour, and—if we’re being honest—rock and metal getting shoved to the side like an unwanted side dish at a fancy dinner.

item.title: My Ticket Home to Play First Show Since 2018—Here’s What to Expect
item.description: Let’s be real. Band reunions? They happen. All. The. Time. Some of them feel like a warm, nostalgic hug. Others? Like a desperate cash grab at the last scraps of remember-us-please energy.

item.title: NONPOINT Drummer Hospitalized After Onstage Health Scare
item.description: Sunday night at the Mercury Ballroom? Ended on a tense note. Why? Drummer Robb Rivera’s heart decided to test its own limits—dangerously high beats-per-minute (like it was auditioning for a drum solo).

item.title: Slipknot's Look Outside Your Window Finally Set for 2025 Release
item.description: Slipknot’s Look Outside Your Window is like Bigfoot. Always talked about. Never seen. But now, after nearly 20 years of “soon, we swear,” the album might actually happen.

item.title: System of a Down Tease Fans with Cryptic 'Chop Suey!' Post
item.description: The legendary metal misfits have stirred the pot again. Hot on the heels of announcing three summer shows with heavyweights like KoRn, Avenged Sevenfold, and Deftones, they pulled a classic move: double the dates, double the hype.

item.title: Jim Root Pushes for Slipknot’s "Look Outside Your Window" Release
item.description: The wait for Look Outside Your Window has dragged on so long, it’s practically become folklore at this point. A decade or more of teasing, false promises, and cryptic updates, and here we are, still empty-handed.

item.title: Courtney LaPlante: "Women Have More Chances Than Ever" to Win a Grammy
item.description: When you’ve been around the block as long as I have, you get used to hearing musicians gush about their “most ambitious project yet.” But Courtney LaPlante, frontwoman of Spiritbox, might actually have a point with her upcoming album, Tsunami Sea, dropping March 7, 2025, via Pale Chord and Rise Records.

item.title: Linkin Park’s From Zero Debuts Globally at No. 1, Lands No. 2 in the U.S.
item.description: Linkin Park’s latest release, From Zero, has made waves globally, though not without its share of quirks. The album, featuring new vocalist Emily Armstrong, hasn’t escaped controversy—her ties to the Cult of Scientology and all the thetanic baggage that comes with it have kept the gossip wheels turning.

item.title: Linkin Park’s Mike Shinoda: “Our New Lineup Came Together Naturally”
item.description: Linkin Park is back. New album (listen below). New lineup. Same vibe. This one’s called “From Zero”, which feels like a bit of an oversell for a band that’s been rehashing itself since 2017.

item.title: Watch: Brandon Toews Masters LINKIN PARK’s From Zero in Record Time
item.description: Linkin Park has thrown their latest creation, From Zero, into the wild, and someone thought it’d be a good idea to see if a drummer could tackle the whole thing on the fly.

item.title: Linkin Park’s Mike Shinoda Talks Brad Delson’s Tour Absence
item.description: Linkin Park’s reunion, complete with a fresh album release last Friday, has been making waves. Yet, the band’s current lineup feels like a revolving door. With Chester Bennington’s tragic loss in 2017 and drummer Rob Bourdon sitting this one out, it’s already a scaled-back return.

item.title: Mike Shinoda on Why Brad Delson Isn’t Touring With Linkin Park
item.description: Brad Delson, the longtime six-string maestro of Linkin Park, is still very much part of the band. In the studio, behind the scenes—he’s there, making things happen. But if you were hoping to see him shred live, prepare for disappointment.

item.title: Linkin Park Announces 2025 Global Tour Across 50+ Cities
item.description: It looks like Linkin Park has made good on their not-so-subtle hints and officially announced a globe-trotting tour to support their upcoming album, From Zero, set to drop this Friday.

item.title: Linkin Park Set to Announce Massive World Tour Ahead of From Zero Release
item.description: Linkin Park’s return to the spotlight hasn’t exactly been smooth sailing. Between the internet losing its collective mind over Emily Armstrong’s connection to Scientology and a convicted r@p1st, the band’s comeback was riding a weird mix of hype and controversy.

item.title: Slipknot’s Clown Talks Delays for 'Look Outside Your Window'
item.description: Back in 2024, Shawn “Clown” Crahan of Slipknot confidently announced that the long-teased *Look Outside Your Window* would finally see the light of day this year. Fast forward to November, and here we are: still no album.

item.title: Slipknot’s 2025 European Tour Announced; See Details
item.description: The masters of mayhem in terrifying masks are set to invade Europe again. Slipknot—yes, the band that makes mosh pits feel like a full-contact sport—dropped the news on Instagram about their upcoming 2025 tour.

item.title: Linkin Park Announces From Zero Listening Events Across U.S.
item.description: Linkin Park is at it again, boys and girls—this time with listening events scattered across over 100 U.S. record stores for their new album, From Zero. Scheduled for Saturday, November 9, these events give fans a sneak peek at the record before it officially hits shelves on Friday, November 15.

item.title: Slipknot's New 'S' Logo Sparks Outrage Among Fans
item.description: Slipknot has rolled out a batch of limited edition merchandise, and one particular shirt seems to have set off quite the tempest. On the front? The band’s name—classic enough.

item.title: The Surprise You Missed in Korn’s 1997 Track "A.D.I.D.A.S."
item.description: Ever really listened to the breakdown in Korn’s 1997 track “A.D.I.D.A.S.”? And I mean actually listened—ears glued to every sound, every tiny layer. There’s a surprise in there you probably missed.

item.title: Watch: Korn Celebrates 30 Years with Epic Anniversary Concert in Los Angeles
item.description: Nu metal’s elder statesmen, Korn, threw a massive party this past weekend in Los Angeles. Their 30th Anniversary bash at BMO Stadium was less of a concert and more of a nu metal reunion, complete with thousands of fans who still remember when baggy jeans and wallet chains were a statement.

item.title: Korn's Original Drummer David Silveria Opens Up on 30th Anniversary
item.description: David Silveria took to Instagram on October 12 to post the cover of the band’s self-titled debut. It wasn’t just a picture, though. He couldn’t resist sharing some heartfelt words.

item.title: KORN's Debut Album Turns 30: Jonathan Davis Reflects on the Band's Legacy
item.description: Friday, October 11, marked 30 years since KORN unleashed their self-titled debut album (listen below). To commemorate the occasion, Jonathan Davis popped up on social media to share the album cover along with a few nostalgic words: “I can’t believe you’re 30 years old.

item.title: Shavo Odadjian’s Seven Hours After Violet Drops New Single "Cry"; VIDEO
item.description: Shavo Odadjian is back with his new project—SEVEN HOURS AFTER VIOLET—and they’ve just dropped the music video for their latest single, “Cry.” Far from being a System of a Down copycat, this track goes straight into anguish, longing, and all the good ol’ despair you’d expect from a song called “Cry.

item.title: Korn and Adidas Pay Tribute to 1994 with New Superstar Shoes
item.description: Korn and Adidas have once again teamed up, this time with a new Superstar shoe drop. It’s about as surprising as the sun rising—anyone who’s been around long enough knows this collab was practically written in the stars.

item.title: Linkin Park's Mike Shinoda: "This Isn’t a Reunion, It’s a New Chapter"
item.description: Mike Shinoda recently shared more details about Linkin Park’s reformation during an interview with BBC Radio 1’s New Music Show With Jack Saunders. The vocalist and multi-instrumentalist pulled back the curtain on how the band’s new chapter began and what fans can expect moving forward.

item.title: Slipknot and Estate of Joey Jordison Settle Lawsuit Quietly
item.description: Joey Jordison’s estate just tied up its legal battle with Slipknot, but good luck trying to find out what really went down. Lawyers on both sides love keeping things as cryptic as possible.

item.title: Watch: Linkin Park Partners with Riot Games for League of Legends Anthem
item.description: Linkin Park is back, boys and girls. Again. This time, they’ve teamed up with Riot Games for “Heavy Is The Crown,” the official anthem for the League of Legends 2024 World Championship.

item.title: 'Master Of Puppets' Wins Out for Shavo Odadjian in METALLICA Album Showdown
item.description: When Shavo Odadjian, bassist of SYSTEM OF A DOWN, got hit with the impossible question of whether METALLICA’s “Ride The Lightning” or “Master Of Puppets” was the superior album during an interview with Radioactive MikeZ on 96.

item.title: KORN’s Brian 'Head' Welch on Mortality: "I Want to Die in a Bed, Not On Stage"
item.description: Brian “Head” Welch from KORN isn’t buying into the whole “die on stage” fantasy. Asked recently about his 2014 comment—where he hinted at retiring by 60—he didn’t exactly backpedal.

item.title: Slipknot Announces 25th Anniversary Reissue of Debut Album
item.description: The year 1999 gave us Slipknot’s chaotic, self-titled debut—an album that didn’t just make waves; it practically slapped the metal world across the face. Now, 25 years later, they’re not only performing to mark the occasion but teasing what sounds like the mother of all reissues.

item.title: Evanescence to Begin Recording New Album in November
item.description: Evanescence—masters of gothic drama and mid-2000s radio dominance—is gearing up to record their next album. When? November. (Mark your calendars, or don’t. Your call.) The news dropped during an interview with 89 A Rádio Rock at Rock In Rio, where the band is currently melting faces.

item.title: Chester Bennington's Mother Accuses Linkin Park of Betrayal
item.description: The rosy glow of Linkin Park’s reunion announcement didn’t last long, did it? The initial buzz around the band’s so-called “new era”—complete with Emily Armstrong as the replacement vocalist—has quickly turned into a storm of controversy and frustration.

item.title: Watch: New Sound, New Faces: Linkin Park Rocks Jimmy Fallon; VIDEO
item.description: Linkin Park hit Jimmy Fallon’s stage last night (17) with their new single, “The Emptiness Machine.” If you missed it, don’t worry. It’s online, complete with enough fog to choke a small village.

item.title: Watch: Korn Performs "Hey Daddy" Live for First Time Since 1999
item.description: Korn pulled a fast one last night. “Hey Daddy”—yep, that’s right. Played live for the first time since 1999. This wasn’t just a random throwback either. September 12, Tampa, Florida.

item.title: Korn Kicks Off 2024 Tour with a Nostalgic Setlist in Tampa
item.description: Korn’s North American tour kicked off last night, and for those of us who’ve been around long enough to remember them actually playing these songs when they first dropped, it was a bit of a nostalgia trip—whether we asked for it or not.

item.title: Jaime Bennington, Chester Bennington's Son Calls Out Linkin Park
item.description: Linkin Park thought they were shaking things up by naming Emily Armstrong their new vocalist, but it’s more like they kicked a hornet’s nest while blindfolded. Fans aren’t just upset—they’re seething.

item.title: MIKE SHINODA Explains Why LINKIN PARK Kept Their Name: "Changing It Would Be Stupid"
item.description: Linkin Park is back, and the headlines are practically writing themselves. New vocalist? Emily Armstrong. New album? From Zero. New tour? It’s happening. But of course, with all this change, the question isn’t just what they’re doing—it’s why.

item.title: Cedric Bixler-Zavala Calls Out Linkin Park's New Vocalist Amid Controversy
item.description: Ok I know, if you’re tired of hearing about Linkin Park, this week’s been a real test of patience. And for those of us who’ve never cared much for the band to begin with, it’s been even worse.

item.title: Emily Armstrong Responds to Scientology and Danny Masterson Allegations
item.description: Oh yeah babe, the music industry—a place where skeletons in closets don’t just rattle, they throw full-blown mosh pits. Barely two days after Linkin Park revealed their shiny new frontwoman, Emily Armstrong (yes, from Dead Sara) found herself in the middle of a PR dumpster fire.

item.title: Brad Delson Walks Away from Linkin Park’s Reunion—Here’s Why
item.description: Here we go again. Linkin Park just can’t stop throwing curveballs. First, it’s a new singer. Then, a new album. And, of course, the big reunion tour. But now?

item.title: Linkin Park Breaks Silence on Rob Bourdon’s Departure
item.description: If you haven’t already heard, Linkin Park is back. And no, this isn’t some watered-down reunion tour cash grab. The band has recruited Dead Sara’s Emily Armstrong as their new vocalist, with Colin Brittain stepping in on drums.

item.title: Watch: Mushroomhead Fans Clash with Slipknot in 1999 Show
item.description: Back in 1999, the tension between Slipknot and Mushroomhead wasn’t just gossip, it was a full-on warzone. A recently resurfaced video from a Cleveland Slipknot show captures this beautiful disaster in all its chaotic glory.

item.title: Linkin Park is Back with a New Album and Unexpected Vocalist
item.description: Leave it to Linkin Park to make their return a three-ring circus. A flashy new album, a shiny logo, and a brand-new vocalist, Emily Armstrong, were all unveiled during a livestream that pulled over 100,000 viewers on YouTube and an extra 26,000 on Instagram.

item.title: Slipknot’s Touring Playbook is Getting a Shake-Up, Says Corey Taylor
item.description: Slipknot’s endless cycle of tours has always begged the question: how do they breathe between the chaos? For Corey Taylor, who’s juggling Slipknot, solo projects, and Stone Sour, the answer is becoming increasingly clear, he doesn’t.

item.title: Is Lzzy Hale the Future Voice of Linkin Park? Fans Think So
item.description: Linkin Park has been pulling some real grade-A stunts lately. Countdowns leading to… more countdowns. Announcements that announce other announcements. It’s like watching a toddler try to explain a magic trick—it’s messy, pointless, and you’re not even mad, just confused.

item.title: Linkin Park Countdown Ends: What Does 'Be Part of Something' Mean?
item.description: It all started with that bizarre 100-hour countdown plastered across Linkin Park’s socials and website last week. For those who missed the memo, this wasn’t your standard “big announcement” fare—it was more like staring at a ticking clock and wondering if someone accidentally pressed the wrong button.

item.title: Countdown Chaos: Is Deryck Whibley Joining Linkin Park?
item.description: The countdown on Linkin Park’s site is ticking, and fans are losing their minds. Again. What is it this time? A new song? A reunion? Nope. The latest theory says Deryck Whibley from Sum 41 is sliding in as their new frontman.

item.title: Sum 41's Deryck Whibley Responds to Linkin Park Frontman Rumors
item.description: Speculation on the rock and metal rumor mill has been churning at full speed this week. Thanks to some coinciding announcements, the internet collectively decided that Sum 41’s frontman, Deryck Whibley, might be stepping in as the new voice of Linkin Park, filling the irreplaceable shoes of the late Chester Bennington.

item.title: Linkin Park’s Mysterious Countdown Leaves Fans Baffled
item.description: What are they doing? Seriously. Saturday rolls around, and boom—Linkin Park drops a post that’s as exciting as a loading screen. A countdown. Plain white numbers on a black background.

item.title: Slipknot's Sid Wilson Injured in Fire Incident Before Rocklahoma
item.description: Slipknot’s resident turntable wizard, Sid Wilson, found himself trading the spotlight for a hospital bed after a fiery mishap involving an “explosion” left him with burns on his face and arm.

item.title: Korn Invites Fans to Create Art for 30th Anniversary—See How You Can Get Involved
item.description: Seems like Korn is dusting off the nostalgia box and pulling out another fan art contest—this time to mark 30 years of Korn wreaking havoc on the rock scene.

item.title: Mike Shinoda Teases “Exciting Things” for Linkin Park Fans
item.description: Reunions? Overdone. Predictable. (Unless it’s the one band you care about—then it’s “historic” and “world-changing,” right?) For years now, Linkin Park has been the one nu-metal heavyweight keeping quiet, while every other act rides the nostalgia wave like it’s 2001.

item.title: Study Shows Korn Fans Get the Best Value for Their Tickets
item.description: These days, going to a concert is like setting fire to your wallet. Everything is overpriced, and ticket prices are no exception. But who’s ready to fork over an arm and a leg just to stand in a crowd?

item.title: Slipknot’s 25th Anniversary Kicks Off with Nothing After 1999; VIDEO
item.description: Slipknot has been teasing this nostalgia-heavy tour for what feels like forever, and last night in Noblesville, Indiana, they finally unleashed the beast. Their ‘Here Comes the Pain Tour’ is officially underway, celebrating 25 years of their self-titled debut—a record that pretty much defined what it meant to be an angry, sweaty teenager in the late ’90s.

item.title: Phil Labonte: Korn’s Impact on Deathcore Goes Beyond Nu-Metal
item.description: When a band ends up becoming so influential that people start crediting them for launching a whole subgenre, it’s something to take note of. But when a group gets blamed for a genre they don’t even directly belong to?

item.title: Slipknot Reveals Knotfest Argentina and Chile Lineups; See Details
item.description: Slipknot is packing its bags—and masks—for another jaunt through South America, this time with Brazilian powerhouse drummer Eloy Casagrande on the roster. The Knotfest machine is revving up for Argentina and Chile, hot on the heels of announcing Knotfest Brazil.

item.title: Korn Showed Us the Ropes, Mötley Crüe Wanted Us Off the Stage, Says Jacoby Shaddix
item.description: Touring for over two decades brings a lot of memories—some good, some you’d rather forget. When Jacoby Shaddix and Jerry Horton of Papa Roach sat down with Q101, they didn’t hold back on sharing stories from the road.

item.title: Slipknot Celebrates 25 Years at Knotfest Brazil; See Details
item.description: Back in 1999, we were all panicking about Y2K taking down the world’s tech, arguing over a president’s private escapades instead of governmental coups, and gleefully downloading Metallica tracks despite their infamous Napster tantrum.

item.title: Korn's Hits Get a Lo-Fi Makeover, And They Approve
item.description: Korn gave a nod of approval to a recent lo-fi album (listen below) of covers that takes their iconic tracks like “Freak on a Leash” and “Blind” and, let’s be honest, strips them down to something that feels like you should be sipping coffee in some indie café.

item.title: Corey Taylor on Why Slipknot Chose Eloy Casagrande as Their New Drummer
item.description: Slipknot’s decision to bring in Eloy Casagrande, formerly of Sepultura, as their new drummer has sparked plenty of chatter. Let’s be honest—watching his relentless, jaw-dropping drum videos circulating online, it’s hard to argue they didn’t find their guy.

item.title: Clown on New Slipknot Music: “Delivered in a Way You Can’t Imagine”
item.description: Slipknot has been on a tear lately. Between nostalgia-drenched 25th-anniversary shows and an endless parade of collaborations (because why not?), the band’s summer could be described as anything but boring.

item.title: Slipknot’s Clown Misses Sonic Temple Due to Dental Surgery
item.description: Slipknot’s lineup has been feeling a bit like a revolving door lately, hasn’t it? Members coming, members going, and the occasional mystery replacement that leaves fans scratching their heads.

item.title: Slipknot Teases New Song Featuring Eloy Casagrande
item.description: Apparently, Slipknot has decided the best way to stay in the headlines is to sprinkle cryptic breadcrumbs all over the internet and let fans fight over the scraps.

item.title: Jim Root: “Slipknot Is Lucky to Have Eloy Casagrande”
item.description: Slipknot’s Jim Root isn’t holding back his admiration for the band’s newest drumming powerhouse, Eloy Casagrande. If Root’s comments are anything to go by, it seems the band practically stumbled into the perfect fit without breaking a sweat—or even auditioning anyone else.

item.title: Slipknot Audition Secrets Revealed by Eloy Casagrande
item.description: Slipknot’s slow-drumroll announcement of Eloy Casagrande as their new drummer didn’t exactly shock anyone. Let’s be real, the fans had already connected the dots ages ago. Still, Eloy opened up in a recent chat with Veja São Paulo (in Portuguese), giving a blow-by-blow of his arduous audition experience.

item.title: Eloy Casagrande’s First Gig with Slipknot Leaves Fans in Awe
item.description: Slipknot’s newest recruit, Eloy Casagrande, hasn’t had much time to catch his breath. His debut as the band’s drummer wasn’t just any gig—it was a small, fiery show staged in a Californian desert venue that probably violates more safety codes than your local dive bar.

item.title: Slipknot Revives 1999 Look at Intimate Anniversary Show; VIDEO
item.description: In a tiny California venue better suited for a rowdy karaoke night than the launch of a metal juggernaut’s 25th anniversary, Slipknot made a dramatic entrance. Decked out in those bright red jumpsuits that defined their early days, the band treated the packed crowd at Pappy + Harriet’s in Pioneertown to a full-on blast from the past.

item.title: Evanescence's Amy Lee Responds to Linkin Park Vocalist Speculation
item.description: Amy Lee. Linkin Park. Together? (Ha, no.) But for a second, it almost felt real, didn’t it? All thanks to Jay Gordon (yes, from Orgy, of all people) who casually mentioned that Linkin Park might—might—be looking for a female vocalist.

item.title: Did Slipknot’s Website Just Confirm Their New Drummer?
item.description: Slipknot’s grand reveal of their mystery drummer is just days away, set to coincide with their live performance at Sick New World. But a few determined internet detectives might have already beaten the band to the punch.

item.title: Brian “Head” Welch Explains Korn’s Shift to Seven-String Guitars
item.description: Korn’s signature seven-string guitar sound didn’t start with some grand plan to revolutionize metal. No, it all began because James “Munky” Shaffer had a thing for Steve Vai, and Brian “Head” Welch?

item.title: Linkin Park Rumored to Return with a Female Lead Singer
item.description: July marks seven years since Chester Bennington’s untimely passing—a moment that shattered not just his family and friends, but the entire world of Linkin Park fans. His death wasn’t just tragic; it was a full stop.

item.title: Brian Welch on Korn's New Album: “The Heaviest in Years”
item.description: Brian “Head” Welch is dropping those familiar lines again—“heaviest stuff in years,” you know the drill. It’s almost like there’s a secret musician handbook, and on page one, right under “never say your best days are behind you,” is this classic line.

item.title: Korn’s Creative Process: Ray Luzier Breaks Down the Band’s Approach
item.description: Korn’s drummer, Ray Luzier, has been pounding the skins for the band since 2007, and he’s got plenty of stories to tell. In a chat with Modern Drummer, Luzier reflected on some of the band’s most memorable moments, from their biggest hits to their more out-there experiments.

item.title: Korn Announces 30th Anniversary Concert with Star-Studded Lineup
item.description: Korn isn’t one to let their 30th anniversary of that self-titled debut just slip by quietly. They’ve decided to throw a massive bash at BMO Stadium in Los Angeles on October 5, 2024.

item.title: Linkin Park Releases "Friendly Fire" Featuring Chester Bennington
item.description: Art has a way of keeping artists alive, doesn’t it? Even when they’re gone, their work lingers on, creating an odd form of immortality. Linkin Park just gave fans a bittersweet reminder of that idea by releasing “Friendly Fire”, an unreleased track featuring the unmistakable vocals of the late Chester Bennington.

item.title: Korn’s Brian “Head” Welch Fights Back Against Mental Health Struggles
item.description: Brian “Head” Welch, the guitarist of Korn, has recently thrown himself into the mental health arena. He’s teamed up with Atlantic Behavioral Health, a fresh facility in Wilmington, Massachusetts.

item.title: Watch: Korn Meets Vanessa Carlton in a Bizarre Mashup
item.description: Just when you thought the world had run out of odd musical combinations, along comes YouTuber mac glocky with a new creation. Fresh off his last “masterpiece”—a mashup of System of a Down and the B-52s—he’s back with another experiment: what happens when you blend Vanessa Carlton’s early 2000s pop hit “A Thousand Miles” with the nu-metal force of Korn?

item.title: Korn's Next Album in 2024 Could Be Their First Without Fieldy
item.description: Korn apparently has some new sounds brewing for 2024, if guitarist Brian “Head” Welch is to be believed. He recently mentioned on The Joe Kingdom Perspective that there’s “new music coming next year,” though it seems like the band is in some kind of self-imposed exile right now, as he put it, “just doing our own thing.

item.title: Amy Lee Reflects on Bring Me to Life's Rap: "Not My Style"
item.description: Amy Lee, the unmistakable voice of Evanescence, hasn’t minced words about her feelings toward the now-iconic rap segment in Bring Me to Life. For two decades, she’s openly expressed her discomfort with the label-driven decision to shoehorn in Paul McCoy’s rap—something neither she nor the band originally envisioned for their breakout hit.

item.title: Brian Welch Reveals Korn’s "Exciting News" Is Coming Soon
item.description: Brian “Head” Welch, guitarist for Korn, has been dropping hints about something “really exciting” on the horizon. Back in December, he mentioned big plans brewing for 2021. Now, in a chat with Kerrang!
